Clarify the meaning of sentences with ambiguous pronouns.

Q: In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: The chief told the counselor that they took the day off.
Options:
(A) The chief took the day off
(B) The counselor took the day off
(C) Ambiguous
A: (A)

Q: In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: The manager sent a message to the secretary, but he didn't reply yet.
Options:
(A) The secretary didn't reply yet
(B) The manager didn't reply yet
(C) Ambiguous
A: (A)

Q: In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: Bailey will plan to meet the director at his office
Options:
(A) It will be Bailey's office
(B) It will be the director's office
(C) Ambiguous
A: (C)

Q: In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: Bailey planned to meet the director at his office

   The antecedent of the pronoun "he" is the secretary, as the sentence is describing the secretary's action of not replying.

3. Bailey will plan to meet the director at his office.
   This sentence is ambiguous, as it is unclear whether the office belongs to Bailey or the director. The use of the future tense "will plan" does not provide enough information to determine the antecedent of the pronoun "his."

4. Bailey planned to meet the director at his office.
   This sentence is also ambiguous, as it is unclear whether the office belongs to Bailey or the director. The use of the past tense "planned" does not provide enough information to determine the antecedent of the pronoun "his."

In summary, the antecedent of the pronoun in the first sentence is the chief, in the second sentence is the secretary, and in the third and fourth sentences is ambiguous.
